snapshot.snapshot_commit: Merge pull request #116: bump openai from 2.53.0 to 3.3.1
review_method: GitHub repository metadata, source files, issue bodies/comments, pull-request state and CI check results
No local clone or test execution was possible in the review environment
snapshot.confidence_note: Repository facts are pinned to the snapshot SHA. Recommendations are analytical judgments and should be revalidated against the current head before application.

decisions.title: What should v0.1 prove?
decisions.question: Choose the public evidence boundary for the first measured release.
decisions.context: The runtime supports invoices and UK job postings across two providers, but only invoices currently have reviewed fixtures. A two-domain claim without a job corpus is not defensible.

options.label: Measured two-domain v0.1
options.summary: Review 30-40 fixtures per domain, run both providers, and publish one frozen benchmark.
options.tradeoffs: Best proof and strongest portfolio story; human review is the critical path.

options.label: Invoice evidence preview first
options.summary: Publish a clearly labelled invoice-only development benchmark while job fixtures are prepared.
options.tradeoffs: Faster and honest, but the README must stop implying two-domain measured coverage.

options.label: No measured release yet
options.summary: Keep the repository as an engineering-complete prototype until both corpora are ready.
options.tradeoffs: No misleading evidence, but delays the project’s main differentiator and lets maintenance consume attention.

decisions.title: How should failures affect accuracy?
decisions.question: Choose the benchmark accounting model before any paid result is published.
decisions.context: The current scorer marks every field on a failed extraction as missed, including fields expected to be null. That conservatively penalizes failures but corrupts null semantics.

options.label: Layered request → extraction → semantic metrics
options.summary: Track infrastructure, accepted extraction and semantic correctness separately; add strict end-to-end document success.
options.tradeoffs: Most honest and diagnostic; requires a modest scorer refactor.

options.label: Treat every failure as all fields missed
options.summary: Keep the current conservative single denominator.
options.tradeoffs: Simple, but null/hallucination metrics become semantically wrong.

options.label: Score successful records only
options.summary: Exclude all failed extractions from semantic metrics.
options.tradeoffs: Clean semantic table but easy to game unless accepted-extraction rate is equally prominent.

decisions.title: What is the hallucination denominator?
decisions.question: Choose the headline definition for invented values.
decisions.context: Dividing hallucinations by all fields can make a model that invents every absent field look acceptable when most fields are populated.

options.label: Expected-null opportunities as headline
options.summary: Report hallucinated / expected-null opportunities, with the old all-fields rate only as context.
options.tradeoffs: Intuitive and comparable; requires tracking null-correct matches separately.

options.label: Conditional rate only
options.summary: Remove the all-fields rate entirely.
options.tradeoffs: Cleanest signal but breaks continuity with current report shape.

options.label: Keep all-fields denominator
options.summary: Preserve current implementation.
options.tradeoffs: Low implementation cost, weak interpretability.

decisions.title: How deeply should nested invoice items be scored?
decisions.question: Choose whether line_items remains one all-or-nothing top-level field.
decisions.context: A single typo in one line item currently turns the entire list into one mismatch, hiding whether descriptions, quantities or prices are the real weakness.

options.label: Top-level plus path-level
options.summary: Keep whole-list exactness and add index-aligned nested path metrics.
options.tradeoffs: Diagnostic without fuzzy matching; assumes item order is stable.

options.label: Top-level only
options.summary: Preserve line_items as one exact field.
options.tradeoffs: Simple and strict, but poor debugging signal.

options.label: Fuzzy item alignment
options.summary: Match line items by semantic similarity or assignment algorithm.
options.tradeoffs: Handles reordered items but adds heuristic/judge-like ambiguity too early.

decisions.title: How should transport failures be classified?
decisions.question: Decide whether a connection failure is model failure, skip, or infrastructure failure.
decisions.context: A connect error can happen before the model sees a document, while a read timeout may occur after a paid request was sent. Treating both as semantic misses is misleading.

options.label: Separate infrastructure class with bounded retry
options.summary: Retry provably unsent failures; record ambiguous sent failures; abort if an infrastructure threshold is exceeded.
options.tradeoffs: Accurate but requires explicit exception classification and journal states.

options.label: Score all as extraction failures
options.summary: Any non-2xx/transport event penalizes the model result.
options.tradeoffs: Conservative but conflates service reliability and model quality.

options.label: Skip all transport/provider failures
options.summary: Only score 200 responses.
options.tradeoffs: Inflates apparent quality and conceals reliability.

decisions.title: How durable must a paid run be?
decisions.question: Choose the run artifact and resume strategy.
decisions.context: Preflight and output preservation are improved, but a process crash or interruption can still lose in-memory per-fixture results after paid calls.

options.label: Append-only JSONL journal + frozen manifest + resume
options.summary: Persist each fixture result before the next call; resume only when corpus/config hashes match.
options.tradeoffs: Small amount of code; high protection and auditability.

options.label: Final Markdown only
options.summary: Rely on the current end-of-run report.
options.tradeoffs: Minimal code, unacceptable loss risk for a paid evidence artifact.

options.label: Full SQLite run database
options.summary: Persist runs and results transactionally.
options.tradeoffs: Powerful but more migration/query complexity than the current need.

decisions.title: How should the corpus be built?
decisions.question: Choose the fastest defensible route from 10/0 reviewed fixtures to a credible benchmark.
decisions.context: The DRAFT/REVIEWED gate already allows agents to draft synthetic data without contaminating published numbers.

options.label: Agent-drafted synthetic + human-reviewed real anonymized
options.summary: Use 30-40 fixtures per type, stratified by edge case; keep a roughly balanced job-posting mix.
options.tradeoffs: Best balance of speed and realism; requires human provenance/review work.
agent_actions: Draft synthetic fixtures and coverage matrix

options.label: Synthetic-only first benchmark
options.summary: Publish only synthetic coverage.
options.tradeoffs: Fast and reproducible but weaker evidence of real document messiness.

options.label: Wait for real-anonymized corpus
options.summary: Use only sourced real documents.
options.tradeoffs: Strong realism, slowest route, harder licensing/provenance burden.

decisions.title: How should the full corpus be rehearsed offline?
decisions.question: Choose a deterministic end-to-end rehearsal mechanism.
decisions.context: The production FixtureClient returns one canned response, so it cannot emulate a complete per-fixture run. Echoing expected labels in production routing risks accidental benchmark leakage.

options.label: Test-only content-hash map + in-process ASGI
options.summary: Inject fixture-specific responses only from tests/rehearsal code and drive the real endpoint without a network server.
options.tradeoffs: Safe, fast and complete; needs a test-only adapter.

options.label: Production expected-label echo mode
options.summary: Let FixtureClient load labels and return expected records.
options.tradeoffs: Easy, but creates a dangerous route that can make the benchmark tautological.

options.label: Keep unit tests only
options.summary: Do not rehearse the full endpoint/corpus path.
options.tradeoffs: Leaves expensive orchestration defects to paid runs.

decisions.title: What must a benchmark manifest freeze?
decisions.question: Choose how reproducible and attributable published results must be.
decisions.context: Provider, model, prompt, schema, corpus and prices can all drift while the final Markdown still looks comparable.

options.label: Full machine-readable manifest
options.summary: Freeze repo SHA, build, provider/model, SDKs, prompt/schema/corpus hashes, prices, timeout/retries and budget.
options.tradeoffs: Strong provenance; modest metadata work.

options.label: Human notes in Markdown
options.summary: Record model IDs and date in the report prose.
options.tradeoffs: Easy, but weak against accidental mixed runs and future comparison.

options.label: Rely on future gateway metadata
options.summary: Defer provenance until gateway integration.
options.tradeoffs: Blocks trustworthy results now and assumes the gateway captures every needed field.

decisions.title: What should happen to field_confidence?
decisions.question: Decide whether the presence flag should remain branded as confidence.
decisions.context: The value is 1.0 for non-null and 0.0 for null. It is not calibrated and can be mistaken for model certainty.

options.label: Add field_presence and deprecate field_confidence
options.summary: Preserve compatibility for one version while making semantics honest.
options.tradeoffs: Small response expansion; avoids misleading consumers.

options.label: Keep with caveat
options.summary: Retain the current name and documentation disclaimer.
options.tradeoffs: No break, but the name remains misleading.

options.label: Remove immediately
options.summary: Delete the field before a formal release.
options.tradeoffs: Cleanest contract if no consumers exist; potentially breaks internal callers.

decisions.title: Should obvious job-posting invariants tighten before the baseline?
decisions.question: Decide whether negative salaries and blank required strings remain valid v1 output.
decisions.context: The current schema accepts negative salary numbers and blank strings. There is no published baseline or release artifact yet.

options.label: Tighten job v1 before first baseline
options.summary: Reject negative salaries and blank title/company/location values; leave invoice sign semantics for v2/credit-note design.
options.tradeoffs: Improves truthfulness with limited blast radius; technically mutates v1 before release.

options.label: Create v1.1
options.summary: Preserve v1 exactly and add a new schema version.
options.tradeoffs: Semantically clean but increases registry/corpus/report complexity before first evidence.

options.label: Keep current schema for baseline
options.summary: Benchmark what exists, then fix later.
options.tradeoffs: Avoids churn but freezes obvious invalid states into the first evidence artifact.

decisions.title: When should atomic idempotency reservation be built?
decisions.question: Choose whether concurrent same-key coordination belongs before v0.1.
decisions.context: Sequential replay is correct; concurrent requests can duplicate spend and temporarily violate conflict semantics.

options.label: Keep sequential v1; trigger on multi-worker deployment
options.summary: Document the limitation and add a deployment gate.
options.tradeoffs: Best effort/value balance for current scope.

options.label: Implement pending reservation now
options.summary: Atomically reserve keys and return retry-later or poll.
options.tradeoffs: Stronger semantics, but introduces recovery/lease/timeout complexity.

options.label: Remove idempotency from v0.1
options.summary: Drop the feature until a distributed design exists.
options.tradeoffs: Simplifies runtime but removes valuable spend protection already built.

decisions.title: How may the service be exposed?
decisions.question: Choose the production network boundary.
decisions.context: The service has no auth, tenant isolation or public rate limiting. The design expects a gateway to own these controls.

options.label: Gateway/reverse-proxy only
options.summary: Bind privately, terminate TLS, authenticate, rate-limit and enforce budgets upstream.
options.tradeoffs: Matches architecture and minimizes duplicate control-plane code.

options.label: Direct service with minimal auth
options.summary: Add a simple API key middleware inside the service.
options.tradeoffs: Faster standalone exposure but duplicates future gateway ownership and needs secret rotation.

options.label: Expose port 8200 publicly
options.summary: Use the current Compose port mapping as the public endpoint.
options.tradeoffs: Not recommended: unauthenticated paid calls and untrusted PDF parsing become internet-facing.

decisions.title: How should the shared deny floor be proven?
decisions.question: Resolve the mismatch between vendored files, current settings and claimed runtime wiring.
decisions.context: A T2 declaration exists and the vendored floor is current, but committed settings no longer wire local PreToolUse. A global adapter may be intentional, yet the repository cannot currently prove it.

options.label: Prove global adapter + pin bytes + gated matrix
options.summary: Document the adapter, verify digests quickly in CI, run the large matrix on relevant changes/schedule.
options.tradeoffs: Preserves central wiring and repository evidence.
agent_actions: Add audit script and filtered workflow

options.label: Restore repository-local PreToolUse wiring
options.summary: Make the repository self-contained again.
options.tradeoffs: Clear provenance, but may double-run or conflict with global hooks.

options.label: Remove vendored floor entirely
options.summary: Rely solely on global tooling.
options.tradeoffs: Reduces repo noise but loses portable evidence and offline auditability.

decisions.title: How should status drift be prevented?
decisions.question: Choose a single source of truth for implementation status and measured claims.
decisions.context: STATUS, PLAN, ADRs, CLAUDE and issue bodies now disagree on coverage floors, API shapes, provider state and completed work.

options.label: Canonical state file + generated summaries
options.summary: Maintain one machine-readable project state and generate status tables/checks from it.
options.tradeoffs: Small tooling cost; greatly reduces repeated narrative drift.
agent_actions: Add state schema, drift check and docs sync

options.label: Manual documentation sweep
options.summary: Update each document now without tooling.
options.tradeoffs: Fast short-term, likely to drift again.

options.label: Leave historical docs as-is
options.summary: Rely on code and README only.
options.tradeoffs: Agents will continue making decisions from stale authority material.

decisions.title: What is the licensing posture?
decisions.question: Choose whether GPL remains the long-term adoption model.
decisions.context: The current service is GPL-3.0-only, while pre-12-August versions retain MIT grants. A network service boundary reduces some embedding concerns, but library reuse and enterprise adoption may still be affected.

options.label: Keep GPL through measured v0.1; review before promotion
options.summary: Avoid another immediate licensing churn while evidence is unfinished.
options.tradeoffs: Stable now; requires an explicit go-to-market decision later.
human_actions: Review intended adopters and commercial model

options.label: Move future releases to permissive
options.summary: Optimize for reuse and portfolio adoption.
options.tradeoffs: Broader adoption potential, less reciprocal protection; relicensing authority must be clear.

options.label: Dual-license/commercial option
options.summary: Keep an open version while offering alternative terms.
options.tradeoffs: Flexible but adds governance and sales/legal overhead disproportionate to current traction.

decisions.title: When should invoice.v2 begin?
decisions.question: Choose the trigger for nullable subtotal and adjustment fields.
decisions.context: The v2 needs are real, but building them before v1 evidence increases scope and splits the corpus.

options.label: After v1 baseline and error review
options.summary: Use measured failures and real fixtures to shape v2.
options.tradeoffs: Evidence-driven and lowest rework.

options.label: Start v2 in parallel now
options.summary: Design and implement nullable subtotal, shipping, discount and rounding immediately.
options.tradeoffs: Addresses known limits sooner but delays the main benchmark and doubles fixture work.

options.label: Keep narrow invoice.v1 permanently
options.summary: Treat unsupported invoice structures as explicit non-goals.
options.tradeoffs: Very simple, but limits practical invoice coverage.

decisions.title: Should extract-api become a release-gate workload?
decisions.question: Choose the project’s strongest medium-term role.
decisions.context: The repository already has deterministic schema validation, two providers, cost/latency tracking and a corpus. That is unusually well suited to regression gating.

options.label: Package as LLM Release Gate workload
options.summary: Promote a human-approved baseline and enforce relative regressions on quality, hallucination, cost and latency.
options.tradeoffs: High reuse and strategic value; thresholds need measured data first.

options.label: Build gate integration before baseline
options.summary: Create framework integration immediately.
options.tradeoffs: Can structure the work, but risks designing thresholds without evidence.

options.label: Keep standalone benchmark
options.summary: Do not integrate with wider release tooling.
options.tradeoffs: Simpler repo, leaves substantial platform leverage unused.

decisions.title: What should happen to dependency PR #119?
decisions.question: Choose the immediate branch hygiene action.
decisions.context: The PR is mergeable and its lint/types/tests, Docker build, secret scan and auto-merge checks are green. It upgrades the OpenAI SDK from 3.3.1 to 3.6.0 among smaller updates.

options.label: Merge now, then run provider-seam canary before paid benchmark
options.summary: Clear maintenance before substantive benchmark work.
options.tradeoffs: Low risk; the paid path still deserves a small canary because SDK mocks cannot prove live compatibility.
agent_actions: Merge/rebase, run gates, add canary to paid-run checklist

options.label: Hold until after benchmark
options.summary: Freeze dependencies before evidence work.
options.tradeoffs: Avoids churn but benchmarks an already superseded dependency set and leaves a green PR hanging.

options.label: Close the update
options.summary: Keep current pins.
options.tradeoffs: No demonstrated reason; increases maintenance debt.

decisions.title: How often should paid evaluation run?
decisions.question: Choose a sustainable benchmark cadence.
decisions.context: A full two-provider corpus on every PR is expensive and noisy, while purely manual runs allow regressions to accumulate.

options.label: Offline gates every PR, small paid canary on relevant changes, full run on release
options.summary: Use representative fixtures for paid drift detection and the full corpus for baseline promotion.
options.tradeoffs: Good cost/signal balance; requires fixture strata and change detection.

options.label: Full paid corpus every PR
options.summary: Maximum immediate signal.
options.tradeoffs: High cost, provider variance and secret-management burden.

options.label: Manual runs only
options.summary: No automated paid evaluation.
options.tradeoffs: Cheapest but weakest regression control.
